title: 5 Banks With Dependable Passive Income Dividends That Could Prosper as Rates Rise
detail:
5 Banks With Dependable Passive Income Dividends That Could Prosper as Rates Rise
Lee Jackson
Wed, November 18, 2026 at 12:11 PM MST 8 min read
C
USB
KEY
PNC
WFC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Quick Read

Citigroup and PNC lead the dividend raises, up 12% and 18%, while Citigroup's payout ratio sits near 24% of earnings.

Rising rates widen bank profit spreads: U.S. Bancorp's net interest margin climbed to 2.84% from 2.75%, as assets reprice faster than funding costs.

Every bank slashed its dividend in the financial crisis, yet payout ratios of 24% to 46% now leave room to keep paying.

The biggest 401k decisions tend to get made once and never revisited: when to roll it over, what to hold inside it, and when to start taking money out. That is exactly what the report: 401k & IRA Tips and Answers was created to address, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

Interest rates are rising again, putting bank dividend payers back in focus for income investors. The Federal Reserve raised the upper bound of its target range to 4.00% on September 17, 2026, up from 3.75%. The 10-year Treasury yield stood at 5.06% on November 18, compared with 4.12% a year earlier, after topping out at 5.31% on October 5. This matters to bank shareholders because of net interest income (NII), the gap between what a bank earns on loans and securities and what it pays depositors.

YinYang / Getty Images

When asset yields rise faster than deposit costs, that spread widens, and the extra profit funds dividend increases. Four of the five banks below raised their quarterly payouts in 2026. The fifth has held its payout steady.

All five banks slashed their dividends during the 2008 to 2009 financial crisis, and one of them cut again in 2020. Each bank's case rests on its record since the recovery, its current earnings coverage, and its capital levels.

Citigroup: A 12% Raise Backed by a Low Payout

Citigroup (NYSE: C) yields 2.27% at a recent price of $118.20. In 2026, it raised its quarterly dividend from $0.60 to $0.67, which management called a 12% increase.

Dividend safety: Trailing diluted EPS of $10.26 compares with $2.47 in trailing dividends per share, which works out to a payout ratio of roughly 24%. CET1 capital (common equity tier 1, a bank's core loss-absorbing capital) was 12.8% in the third quarter, about 120 basis points above the 11.6% requirement. Citi also bought back $13.3 billion of stock year to date. The crisis cut was severe: the payout fell from $0.54 a quarter in 2007 to $0.01 by 2009 and stayed there through 2014. Since the recovery began in 2015, the dividend has not been reduced. It held at $0.51 from 2020 through 2022 and has gone up every year since.

title: Citi Bank Slashes Dell And HPE Price Targets Ahead Of Earnings
detail:
Citi Bank Slashes Dell And HPE Price Targets Ahead Of Earnings
Nauman Khan
Wed, November 18, 2026 at 11:00 AM MST 1 min read
C
DELL
HPE
CSCO
ANET
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Citi (NYSE:C) cut its price targets on Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE) but still named both its top IT hardware picks ahead of earnings.

Analyst Asiya Merchant kept Buy ratings, lowering Dell's target to $550 from $600 and HPE's to $80 from $92. Those levels imply gains of about 70% and nearly 74%, respectively.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with C.

Is C fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

C GF Value chart

Citi pointed to its quarterly survey of chief information officers, checks with resellers and upbeat comments from Cisco (CSCO), Arista Networks (ANET) and CDW (CDW), which suggest a broad upgrade cycle in business IT.

Demand for AI infrastructure also remains strong, the bank said, though it flagged worries about peak AI demand and weaker PC sales.

Dell shares have dropped more than 30% in three months, a level Citi views as attractive.
